scope: Woodford, Interest and Prices, Chapter 6: Inflation Stabilization and Welfare, with Appendix E. Second-order welfare approximations in two layers: exact polynomial identities with explicit terms independent of policy and explicit third-order remainders, and a one-parameter Taylor bridge from actual expected utility with O(eps^3) remainders and welfare-ranking corollaries. Approximation theory (1.2)-(1.10) corrected; Props 6.1-6.5 and the exact Calvo dispersion identities; Prop 6.6 with corrected weights; the case for price stability; transactions frictions and the zero lower bound with a proved two-constraint KKT theorem (Props 6.7-6.9); asymmetric disturbances and sticky wages (Props 6.10-6.13); cost-push shocks; large distortions with (5.1) corrected and the second-order AS (5.4) derived from the Calvo model (Props 6.14-6.15).
source: Michael Woodford, Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy, Princeton University Press, 2003, Chapter 6, pp. 381-463, and Appendix E, pp. 692-708.
